title: 2 Corinthians Bible Quiz - Chapter 1
description: Ten questions on 2 Corinthians 1: the God of all comfort, the affliction in Asia, and the promises of God that are Yes in Christ.

questions.text: Who is named with Paul in the opening greeting of this letter?
questions.explanation: The letter opens from Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, and Timothy our brother.

answers.text: Silvanus
Titus
Apollos
Timothy

questions.text: How is God described in verse 3?
questions.explanation: Verse 3 blesses the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and God of all comfort.

answers.text: The God of the living and the dead
The Father of mercies and God of all comfort
The Father of lights and God of peace
The God of order and of silence

questions.text: Why does God comfort them in all their affliction, according to verse 4?
questions.explanation: Verse 4 says God comforts us in all our affliction so that we may be able to comfort those who are in any affliction, through the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God.

answers.text: So that they may be able to comfort others in any affliction
So that they may never be afflicted again
So that they may boast before the assemblies
So that they may be sent on to Judea

questions.text: Where did the affliction happen that weighed them down so much that they despaired even of life?
questions.explanation: The writer tells them about the affliction which happened in Asia, where they were weighed down exceedingly, beyond their power, so much that they despaired even of life.

answers.text: In Judea
In Achaia
In Asia
In Macedonia

questions.text: According to verse 9, in whom were they not to trust, and in whom were they to trust?
questions.explanation: Verse 9 says they had the sentence of death within themselves, so that they should not trust in themselves, but in God who raises the dead.

answers.text: Not in men, but in the law
Not in themselves, but in God who raises the dead
Not in the assembly, but in the apostles
Not in their suffering, but in their own wisdom

questions.text: How does the writer say the Corinthians were helping together on their behalf?
questions.explanation: He says they were helping together on his behalf by their supplication, so that thanks might be given by many persons on their behalf.

answers.text: By their supplication
By keeping silent about his affliction
By writing letters of commendation
By travelling with him to Judea

questions.text: What journey had the writer determined on in his confidence toward them?
questions.explanation: He was determined to come first to them, to pass from them into Macedonia, to come again from Macedonia to them, and to be sent forward by them on his journey to Judea.

answers.text: To sail from Corinth straight to Jerusalem with the gift
To winter in Corinth and then travel on to Galatia
To come to them, pass into Macedonia, return to them, and be sent on to Judea
To stay in Asia until the affliction there had ended

questions.text: Who, besides the writer, is named as having preached the Son of God among them?
questions.explanation: Verse 19 says the Son of God, Jesus Christ, was preached among them by us, by me, Silvanus, and Timothy.

answers.text: Titus and Apollos
Cephas and James
Aquila and Priscilla
Silvanus and Timothy

questions.text: What does verse 20 say about the promises of God?
questions.explanation: Verse 20 says that however many are the promises of God, in him is the Yes, and therefore also through him is the Amen, to the glory of God.

answers.text: In him is the Yes, and through him the Amen, to the glory of God
They are Yes and no, as men purpose according to the flesh
They are sealed with a veil until the Lord returns
They belong to the old covenant only

questions.text: What does the writer say about his relation to their faith in verse 24?
questions.explanation: Verse 24 says: We don't control your faith, but are fellow workers with you for your joy. For you stand firm in faith.

answers.text: He is the judge of their faith and will examine them
He does not control their faith, but is a fellow worker with them for their joy
He has handed their faith over to Timothy to guard
He will come to Corinth to correct their faith himself
